title: Small Fixes
items: Scythes have a new model (the Reaper's own scythe is unchanged): a dark, grooved iron blade with a toothed inner edge, an old skull at the joint and a bent, leather-wrapped wooden shaft.
The Reaper's rites now have their own icons instead of borrowing other classes' pictures.
Joining a friend's party late no longer leaves your game half-started: you show as online to friends and get update notices again.
Item tooltips no longer squeeze a stat's name down to one letter per line when its explanation is long.
The Reaper's soul bag now fills when a soul actually reaches her, not the moment an enemy dies.
The F3 performance monitor now sits in the bottom-right corner, out of the way of the HUD and windows, and you can click through it.

New test weapon for the Reaper, the Scythe of Undeath (Smithing, level 1: one copper ingot and old bones): Haunting Wraith raises three wraiths in a cone, every soul in her bag adds damage and cuts damage taken, and a soul gained with a full bag casts a free Haunting Wraith.

Haunting Wraith has no cooldown now, so you can cast it again while you have 5 souls to spend. With the Scythe of Undeath, every soul that lands on a full bag casts its own free Wraith, with no one-a-second limit.
Haunting Wraith no longer leaves a glowing ring on the ground under it; soul wisps rise off its path instead.
Toxic corpse pools now hurt at the level of the area they are in, not always like level 1: a deeper area's pools hit as hard as its monsters.
A plague bearer thrall now leaves its rot pool where it falls: it slows and withers the monsters standing in it for 5 seconds.
The Mourning Bell now works: each hit of your wraiths heals you and the party members near them by 2% of their health.
The last few seconds of gathering are no longer lost when you quit, log out or switch character: they are paid and counted before the game closes.
Easy auto combat now walks round gravestones instead of getting stuck in the gaps between them.

Seven Covenant counsel tips that never appeared now show, each once at its moment: the Depths (going down alone, each floor, elites with extra affixes, the fifth floor's chest), the Week's Omen, a new weapon line, a set bonus switching on, and the loadouts tip when you learn your sixth rite.
If your connection to a party drops, the game now offers to take you back: a notice and a Rejoin button in the Social window (O) for 5 minutes. It never joins by itself.
Friends now see you online from the moment you sign in, at character select and while the world loads, not only once you are in the world.

The Altar of Ascension is quiet until Ascension returns redesigned: it no longer opens its old window, the Prior no longer points you to it, and party and friends lists show the difficulty without Heat.
Fewer hitches the first time you cast a spell: starting a game or saving Settings no longer throws away the effects the loading screen prepared.
In a party, every area a player is fighting in now gets its own waves; before, only the host's area did, so a friend fighting in another area met no new enemies.
Co-op: a guest's waystone map (M) now lists the areas open in the host's world, where the party plays, instead of the guest's own.
Co-op: a guest now sees a damage number for every blow of the thralls, as the host does, not just the one that kills.
Co-op: a guest now gets its own first-kill bonus and trophy for a boss (the server checks your own record), not just the host.
Co-op: a guest can now call a boss Empowered with a Covenant Seal from its own bag at the altar and claim the prize, and its screen dims for Nightfall along with the host's world.
Joining a friend's party after you have woken a boss in your own game no longer fails with a "co-op data mismatch".

In a party, you can now wake any boss your host has opened, even one in an area you have not opened yourself yet; you still pay with your own soul shards (or your own Covenant Seal for an Empowered boss).
Joining a party late no longer sometimes leaves the doors to areas the host has opened shut in front of you.
The Plague Doctor's flask pool is now drawn on the ground for as long as it hurts, so you can see it and step out.
When a boss resets after a wipe, its pools and burning ground vanish at once instead of lingering.
Settings now says the Catacomb Depths are a solo descent and the stair turns a party away, instead of saying a party steps out and rejoins.
"Point to it on the minimap" works again: the minimap pings the spot the Next-step box suggests.
In the Hollow Graves the Next-step box now leads you to the Gravedigger King first (gather his soul shards, then wake him at the King's Grave); the Ossuary seal comes after he falls.
Your thralls now wear your Legion kit: the armour piece colours their chests and hands, the weapon piece their blades and staves.

Each discipline's thralls now look like their own legion: the Ossuary's bone sentinels, the Gravecaller's legionnaires, the Rotweaver's plague thralls and the Mourner's wraiths. In a party everyone sees each owner's look.
Water ripples: rings spread from your steps in puddles and flooded halls, where bodies fall in water, from the Fen Wisp's pulse and the Mire Mother's rings.
The Sanctum's candles gutter as the Bell-Sworn Prelate grows stronger: the west ones die in its second phase, the east ones in its third, and they light again when the fight starts over or ends.

title: Smoother First Moments
items: The first item that drops in a session, and the first time you equip new gear, a cape or a flying pet, no longer cause a brief hitch: the loading screen now prepares them.
Haunting Wraith now strides along twice as fast, as a big see-through ghostly ghoul (a stand-in until it gets its own model).

title: The Crypts Stir Again
items: Grave Surges are back: after a while in a combat area, a crypt nearby cracks open and three waves of the dead climb out. Kill most of them before it seals (about 20 seconds) for a guaranteed relic and bonus gold.
If the game ever crashes in a fight, its automatic crash report now says exactly where, so we can fix it faster.
The benchmark window now says where your finished runs go: the game's benchmark page.

When you stop playing, the game sends us a small report of how smoothly it ran (frame times, your graphics card and preset) and where you played. Nothing personal; it helps us make the game run well on every PC. The numbers are on the site's play reports page.
The game now arrives with many of its shaders already prepared, so the first start after an update loads faster.
New Reaper spell, Haunting Wraith (Grimoire): a huge wraith rises at your feet and walks toward the cursor, hurting every enemy it touches. 5 souls, 14s cooldown.

title: Rebuilt from the Bones
items: Death Muffin has been rebuilt underneath: the same game, much faster. The biggest fights run about three times faster on a strong PC, and older PCs gain even more.
Big fights stay smooth: whole crowds of enemies and thralls are now drawn by the graphics card, and every effect is prepared on the loading screen so nothing stutters the first time you cast it.
Every area has baked lighting, and every graphics setting from Low to Ultra now uses the high-quality renderer.

Ascension is resting while it is redesigned: the Altar of Ascension, vows, heat, Ashes and Covenant Boons are gone for now (with them the boon's extra thrall). Your Ascension progress is kept safe on the server; nothing is lost.
Co-op: a party guest can now use waystones and the recall (T).
The Reliquary no longer misses clicks while loot comes in during a fight.
This update is one bigger download (about 510 MB of art). Updates after it are small again.
Something look or feel wrong? Send it with the bug report button in Settings.

title: A Steadier Soundtrack
items: Fixed a rare crash in the game's sound: once in a while, setting up or re-routing sound channels while sounds were playing could close the game.

title: The Biggest Fight
items: The Benchmark has a new Full Party fight: 72 enemies, 32 thralls and the room's boss, the biggest fight the game can make. It measures how your PC handles a full four-player party.

title: Bring Your Own Potions
items: Joining a friend's party, your belt now works: Q drinks a healing flask, Z / X drink your elixir and tonic, and meals heal you, all from your own bag.
A party member can now wake a boss at its altar with their own soul shards, not just the host.
The Reaper has a new look: a hooded figure in torn purple-and-black cloth with a bone shoulder and a lantern, instead of metal armor.

title: The Ceiling Holds
items: Level 999 is the cap, and the game now knows it: no more "Level 1000" announcement popping up after every kill at 999.
Party kills in a ground you haven't opened yet now count the same in the game as on the server.

title: Lighter, Smoother, Safer
items: Smaller updates: the game's art and sound now ship as their own file, so most future updates download about 14 MB instead of 280 MB. This update is the last big one.
Co-op now runs over a faster connection when your network allows it, so a dropped packet no longer makes everyone stutter. If it can't connect, co-op works the way it did before.
If the game ever crashes, it now sends the devs a crash report with your game log the next time you play, and tells you it did.

title: Same Page
items: If a new version comes out while you're playing, the game now tells you right away, so you can restart from the launcher to update.
Parties now need everyone on the same version. Joining a friend on a different one tells you who needs to restart from the launcher, instead of joining and acting strangely.

title: Come Back Anytime
items: Leaving a party no longer locks you out of it: rejoin and you earn XP, gold and loot again right away.
New parties are Open by default, so friends can hop straight in with Join. Tick Closed when hosting if you want invite-only.
The Vault's Sort, Take and Deposit buttons now update the window as soon as the server answers, instead of after extra refreshes.

title: Heat That Adds Up
items: Fixed the Plague Saint's glowing green feeding beams from her Plague Doctors piling up and staying on screen for minutes; they now fade after a second.
Fixed the Professions window saying you had no tool when your hatchet, pickaxe, rod or spade was on the tool belt.
Self vows now pay: every vow you swear on yourself (Frail Vessel, Famished Rites, Brittle Dead, Dry Cellar) adds to your gold and XP bonus, solo and in a party.
In a party you earn at the host's heat plus your own self vows, so taking on more personal handicaps pays more than your friends get.
The host's heat and difficulty now show everywhere a party does: your friends list, party invites, the Party window and above the party list on your screen (with "+N yours" for your own self vows).
Runes socketed by party members now work on their spells in your world.
Ticking gear in the Bone Grinder no longer scrolls the list back to the top.
Opening the Vault or the bag no longer flashes empty first: your gear, bag and the last Vault contents show straight away.

title: The Server Keeps Your Bag
items: Your Reliquary now lives entirely on the server: sorting, drinking, selling and every other bag change is done by the server, so items can no longer vanish or come back from a save that arrived late.
Sort now merges your potions, elixirs and meals into full stacks too.

title: Every Coin Counted
items: Summoned bosses now always pay their full XP and gold, however fast you summon them.
Fixed: while hosting a party, Catacomb Depths floor clears and boss kills could go uncounted by the server.
The server now keeps a record of every gold, XP and soul shard change, so lost progress can be traced and given back.

title: Honest Gold
items: Selling now happens on the server, and affixed gear sells for its full affixed price.
Contract rewards and laborers' earnings are paid straight into your gold by the server.
Your gold and level can no longer be knocked back by a save that arrived late.

title: Boss Rush
items: Fixed: the Vault's Deposit materials and Take materials buttons no longer move potions, elixirs and tonics; they only move materials and runes.
Summon bosses back to back as fast as you like: every boss you pay for now always drops its loot, and so does every boss your party's host summons while you are with them.
Fixed: after a fast run of Prelates, boss loot could be refused when you picked it up.
You can now rebind the performance overlay to another key in Settings > Controls (it stays on F3 until you change it).
Fixed: in co-op, doors showed as shut for guests even though they could walk through them. Guests now see the host's doors, open or sealed, and a seal breaking opens the door for them too.

title: Fair Loot, Finished
items: New Reaper spell, Scythe Weave: twirl the scythe in a figure eight across the half-circle in front of you, two passes that hit everything in reach. Free, 0.9 second cooldown, and holding its key keeps you weaving. Place it on your bar from the Spellbook (L).
Catacomb Depths: floor rewards and chest finds are now decided by the server too, and still appear the moment you earn them.
Loot can now only reach your bag by picking it up. If the game ever showed you something the server didn't deal, it simply won't land in your bag.
Reaper's Scythe Weave is now a fast single-target strike: it chops down from above onto the nearest enemy, then cuts back up through it, twice as often (0.45 second cooldown).

title: Stronger Together
items: Co-op: when you join someone's party, your own gear, set bonuses, affixes, boons and upgrades now count in their world. Change gear mid-session and the host picks it up.
Co-op: a guest's kills in a higher-level host's world now count properly.
Fixed: a rune could vanish when you picked it up as a party guest.

title: Benchmark Rooms
items: The Benchmark button on character select now opens a setup window: pick the room, the class, the fight size (Light, Standard or Heavy) and the length (Quick or Full). It remembers your last pick.
Every room keeps its own creatures and their abilities, but every enemy has the same health and damage in every room, so kills cost the same everywhere.
The Bell Sanctum with a Gravecaller, Standard size, Full length is the Standard setup: the one whose numbers compare between PCs. Other picks are marked custom.
The results now show kills per minute and a "vs last run" column against your previous run of the same setup (green better, red worse).
Every finished run is added to the new public Benchmarks page on the website, with your name and your PC's graphics card and processor, so we can track performance across updates.
The Reaper's souls are now small glowing green skulls instead of tadpole-shaped wisps, both when they fly to you and when Unleash Souls circles you.

title: Fair Loot
items: The Legion window now shows the new tier and your gold the moment a Reinforce goes through, instead of trailing behind the click.
Fixed: spamming Reinforce up to the max tier left the Legion window showing an old tier and "Already at max tier"; it now refreshes after the last click.
Spamming Reinforce in the Legion window no longer lags: the game now refreshes your stats once after the last click instead of after every one.
Every drop is now decided by the server. Loot still appears the moment an enemy falls; picking an item up checks it with the server, which puts it straight into your bag.
In a party, your drops are rolled for you on your own game, from the host's kills.
Fixed: characters above level 255 had their kills in the level-scaled grounds ignored by the server's checks.
Party chat now dings a short bell when another player sends a message. Your own messages stay silent, and the Interface volume slider in Settings controls it.

title: Safer Saves
items: The server now checks more of what it saves for every character. If it cannot check a save for a moment, it keeps your progress on your PC and tries again, so nothing is lost.
Leaderboard: characters played with the team's testing tools (GM mode) now carry a GM tag.

title: Play With Friends
items: No more party codes. The Friends tab (O) shows who is online, their class and level, where they are and whether they are in a party.
Join a friend's Open party with one click. If their party is Closed, or they are playing solo, click Ask to join: they get a note, and when they accept you go straight in.
Invite a friend from the Friends tab. If you are playing solo, inviting starts a Closed party for you. Invites and requests wait in the Friends tab for 5 minutes, and clicking the note opens it.
Parties are Open (listed, anyone can join) or Closed (only people you invite; friends can ask). Hosts switch between them in the Party tab (F).
Friend requests now arrive while you play: no need to log out and back in to see them.
Reaper: Soul Harvest now doubles the damage of the next spell you cast.
Vault: click an item to see its full card, double-click to move it between your bag and the Vault (Shift+double-click to choose how many).

title: Friends
items: New Social window (O) with a Friends tab: add a friend by the name they log in with. Once they accept, you see each other in the list with the class and level each of you last played.
Friend requests wait for you in the Friends tab (Accept or Decline). If someone asked you while you were away, you get a note when you enter the world.
The Party window is now the Social window's Party tab. F still opens it, and the HUD button is called Social.
Contracts no longer have their own key (O is Social now). Open them from the Acre ledger (P).

title: Learn Your Runes
items: Chat is easier on the eyes: party messages get a violet edge, finds and legendary drops are gold, and system notes are a muted silver.
Runes are now learned instead of carried. A rune still drops into your bag: select it in your Reliquary (I) and click Learn. It is spent and you know it for good.

Every rune you know is a choice for its spell in the Spellbook (L), which lists all of that spell's runes with their rarity (Uncommon, Rare, Epic), even the ones you have not found: click a learned one to put it in, or Empty the socket. Swapping no longer needs bag room, but only works out of combat.
A rune you already have (learned, in your bag or in the Vault) never drops for you again. Duplicates no longer turn into soul shards or other runes.
Unlucky streaks end sooner: every elite that leaves no rune makes the next one likelier, up to three times the usual chance, until a rune drops.
Runes already in your sockets are learned for you. Runes in your bag or Vault wait for you to learn them; spare copies can still be kept or ground in the Bone Grinder.
The Heal, Elixir and Tonic slots on the HUD now show the icon of the potion you actually have equipped.
The boss war-drum heartbeat no longer keeps thumping after a boss fight ends in some other way than the boss dying (you die, leave the area, or the boss resets).
Co-op fix: a Reaper who joins someone else's party keeps her Reaper rites (her hotbar had switched to the necromancer's).
New Reaper spell, Soul Harvest: leech every living monster within 9m, gaining 1 soul and some health for each one hit. Free, 5 second cooldown. Place it on your bar from the Spellbook (L).

title: Drop Gear for Your Party
items: Select gear in your Reliquary (I) and press Drop: it lies at your feet until you leave the world. Epic and legendary pieces ask first.
In a party, anyone who was with you when that piece dropped can pick it up. Click it like any loot; the first one to grab it gets it. Gear found before someone joined stays yours alone.
Only gear can be dropped, up to 20 pieces at a time. Anything left on the ground is gone when the session ends.
Fixed the Reliquary window stretching off-screen when you click a piece that replaces several worn items.
Spamming Empower or Quicken no longer lags: the game used to re-read your whole build after every single server reply, now it waits for the last one.

The Spellbook button on the action bar is now a square "Spells" button, lined up with the ability icons and showing its L key underneath like they do. Clicking it (or pressing L) while the Spellbook is open now closes it.

title: Loot: Click to Pick Up
items: Gold and soul shards now go straight to your purse when an enemy dies. One float per fight, no more coins on the ground.

Gear and materials stay on the ground for 3 minutes (was 1 minute). Walking over them no longer picks them up: click a drop and your hero walks over and grabs it. Hover a drop to see its name, hold Alt to see every name, and Alt+click grabs loot in the middle of a fight.

Runes go straight into your bag, and you never get a rune you already own (bag, sockets and Vault count): a duplicate becomes a rune you are missing, and once you own every rune a source can drop it pays 1-3 soul shards instead. A Reaper keeps collecting necromancer runes for a switch back.
Finding a new rune or a legendary posts a line in chat. In a party everyone sees it.
The Settings loot rules (Auto-loot, Sell for gold) are gone. Sell spare gear with Sell all junk in the Reliquary (I).
Vault Deposit all and Deposit materials now leave the largest stack of each belted flask, elixir and tonic in your bag.

title: The Reaper's Full Set Look
items: Soul Harbinger's Raiment now dresses the whole Reaper: from 3 pieces she wears the full green bone armor (hood, glowing ribcage, bone pauldrons, gauntlets and greaves) as one outfit, with the green bone scythe and a soft green glow at her edges. Below 3 pieces the hood shows on its own.
The Reaper's attacks play their own swings again (sweep, slam, throw, channel and summon) instead of one generic swing.

title: Soul Harbinger's Raiment
items: The Reaper's own legendary armor set is in the game: Soul Harbinger's Raiment (Harbinger's Hood, Ribcage, Grasp, Legwraps and Treads). It drops from area bosses like the other legendary sets, and most often for a Reaper.
The Reaper's scythe is bigger and now sits in her hand by the shaft instead of floating beside it.
Wearing it shows the green bone hood with glowing eyes and the ribcage mantle; from 3 pieces your scythe becomes the green bone scythe.

Set bonuses: 2 pieces double Scythe Throw's radius, 4 pieces turn the damage your Unleash Souls does into a shield (a new Unleash refreshes it, it never stacks), 5 pieces leave a Scythe Throw where each soul lands (up to 15).
The Reaper's Reap and Scythe Throw no longer have a cooldown (only their soul cost limits them), and Wraith Walk comes back after 5 seconds instead of 11.

title: Smoother Big Fights and a Benchmark
items: Clicking Empower and Quicken feels snappier: the new tier, cost and gold show on the next frame, and a purchase no longer redoes the vow and boon setup.

Reaper set bonuses are in the code for Soul Harbinger's Raiment (the armor pieces themselves come later): 2 pieces double Scythe Throw's radius, 4 pieces turn the damage your Unleash Souls does into a shield (a new Unleash refreshes it, it never stacks), 5 pieces leave a Scythe Throw where each soul lands (up to 15).

Big fights with lots of loot on the ground run much smoother: in a 30-enemy test fight the frame rate went from about 42 to 87 fps and the long freezes are gone. Soul shards no longer light the ground around them; their crystals still glow.
If the game ever falls far behind, it now slows for a moment instead of freezing up.
Effects, the HUD and the world do less work every frame (same look).

New Benchmark button on the character select screen: it plays the same offline fight on any PC (your characters are not touched) and shows your frame rate and what each part of the picture costs. Copy the result and share it with us. Near the end the fight freezes on purpose while it measures; a banner says so.

title: Fen Herbs in the Sexton's Acre
items: Bog Myrtle (gravedigging 25) and Drowned Lotus (gravedigging 45) now also grow in the Sexton's Acre, so Start AFK and Grave Laborers work for every gravedigging tier.
The Reaper has a new look: a skeletal, rogue-like reaper in medium armor instead of robes.

title: One Character Per Account
items: Work tables, the altar, the vault and other stations now close their window when you walk a few steps away.
Picking a discipline (including from Switch character) now switches your own character to it instead of starting a new level-1 character. Your level, gold and gear stay.
"Don't show tips" now follows your account: turn tips off once and they stay off on every device.
Crafting with Max (or any batch) now shows live progress on the button (Crafting 3/20) instead of looking frozen.
Laborers sent to a post that has no node in the Acre (like level 45 gravedigging) now work the closest lower tier there instead of the level 1 node.
Settings > Display now has a V-Sync switch. Turn it off for lower input delay and frame rates above your screen's refresh rate.

title: Necromancer Look: Real Weapons, Helms and Mantles
items: Reaper Wraith Walk now lets out a high banshee wail as she rushes.

Every necromancer weapon now has its own model in your hand: staves, scythes, wands, sickles, skull foci, mourning bells and grimoires. Bone, iron, gold, hell and moon weapons share a model and differ in metal and glow. The default staff uses the new staff too.

Helms show as a hooded crown over your hero: iron for class sets, silver for ascended sets, copper, iron and silver for crafted helms, a thorned hellsteel crown for legendary sets. Hide helms still hides them.
Wearing the chest piece of a class or ascended set puts that set's mantle on your hero's shoulders.

Wear 3 pieces of a legendary set (Legion Unburied, Colossus Mantle, Requiem Wraiths, Plague Choir) and your hero becomes that set's hero, weapon and all. Take a piece off and you are yourself again. Other players see it too.
The Vault's Take materials and Take all buttons are fast now: they move everything in one go instead of one stack at a time.
Reaper Wraith Walk no longer flings her off screen: she stays on the ground, rushes at an even speed and slips through props and gravestones, stopping only at walls.

title: Necromancer Look: Staff in Hand
items: The staff (and every weapon) now sits in your hero's hand and moves with it: no more staff hinged at the elbow, and casts swing the staff forward instead of leaving it behind.
Gear keeps your robe's own colours: worn pieces tint the trim and edges instead of washing the whole robe.
Weapons glow by rarity (rare, epic and legendary get a stronger halo and drifting motes that streak as you swing), coloured by the weapon's metal or your socketed runes.
Wearing 2+ pieces of a set adds a set aura that grows at 4 pieces; 3+ pieces switch on the set's colours.
Reaper: Unleash Souls now sends every soul (up to 30) out in an even ring first, and only then does each one lock onto an enemy, sharing out the targets instead of all piling onto the nearest one.
Reaper: Unleash Souls no longer snaps the ring back to you before launching; the souls lock on from where the ring ended.

title: Polish Pass: Co-op, Animation and the Reaper
items: Co-op: everyone in a party now shows their real level, and the world scales to the party leader's level instead of whoever happens to be standing closest.
Co-op: bosses gain much less health per extra player (two players: x1.3 instead of x1.8; four: x1.9 instead of x3.4).

Bosses no longer get stuck on walls or on thralls: they slide along walls, find a way round when blocked, and walk through a thrall legion. In co-op a boss keeps one target instead of flipping between players.

Co-op: shared objectives count for the whole party. Every party kill adds to each member's area kills and seals (opening the next ground), even if you are dead or far away, and kills in a ground you haven't opened yourself still count for you. XP and loot are unchanged.
Co-op: players who join a party no longer get boss XP skipped, and the Rotweaver's Soul Harvest meter fills for them.
Co-op: no more sluggish WASD right after joining (joiners now arrive on walkable ground).
Settings has tabs along the top: Co-op and Audio first, then Play, Display, Controls and Account. It remembers the last tab you used.
Switch character (Settings, Account) takes you back to character select without logging in again.

Smoother animation: enemies, thralls and bosses recoil when hit, lunge into their strikes, climb out of the ground when they rise, tip over smoothly when they die, and crowds no longer breathe in step. The necromancer's scythe swing no longer snaps by at 20x speed.
The Reaper always holds her scythe, even with another weapon in her bag.

The Reaper's rites now swing like a scythe: Scythe Sweep and Harvest Spin sweep, Reap slams down, Scythe Throw flicks, Wraith Walk and Soul Burst use the channel and summon poses, and haste speeds the swing up.
Auto combat now plays the Reaper: Scythe Sweep as the filler, souls spent on Reap, Harvest Spin, Soul Burst and Scythe Throw, and Wraith Walk to escape when she is low.
Scythe Sweep hits a third harder.
The game window now just says "Death Muffin".
Reaper: new ability Unleash Souls (R). It lets every soul in your bag go at once; each one hunts the nearest enemy and strikes it, and with no enemies around they circle you until one shows up.

title: The Reaper: Built for the Front Line
items: Wraith Walk turns the Reaper into a large, half-see-through wraith with a faint green glow for the rush: she passes through monsters, takes no damage, and sets everything she passes through alight with a green flame that burns for 5 seconds.

The Reaper can take a hit now: 30% more health than a necromancer, 15% less damage from every blow, and each enemy a scythe swing strikes heals her a little (up to 6% of her health a swing). Wraith Walk's rush can't be hit.
Harvest Spin and the spinning thrown scythe leave a sweeping blade trail, every scythe hit lands with a green impact flash, and Soul Burst slams the ground.
The Reaper has her own portrait on character select.
The Reaper now carries a green-etched scythe in her hand, and Scythe Throw sends the same scythe spinning across the ground.

The Reaper's souls are now her only resource: the energy orb is her soul bag, every rite except the free Scythe Sweep costs souls, and every enemy that dies gives her one. Souls wisp around the corpse for a second before flying to her.

title: Arrange Your Bag and Vault
items: Drag an item onto any bag or Vault slot to put it exactly there: an empty slot takes it, the same item stacks onto it, and a different item swaps places.
Rearrange inside your bag (in the Reliquary or the Vault window) and inside the Vault, or move items between them to the slot you choose.
Hold Shift while dropping a stack to choose how many go to that slot.

title: Sharper Spell Impacts
items: The Settings button "Leave the world" is now called "Logout".
Pressing Esc to clear a keybind no longer closes the Settings window.
Bone Needle, pierce and Scythe hits now land with an animated impact burst, and critical hits flare with a bright ring of rays.
Exhume draws a glowing summoning circle under the corpse as it rises.
The Contagion rune's spread is now a crackling tendril of rot from the dying enemy to the next one.
Settings now has an "Exit game" button at the top, so you can quit from fullscreen without alt-tabbing. It saves first.
The Ossuary Vault now shows your worn gear beside the Reliquary, laid out like the Reliquary's gear slots.

In the Vault, the Deposit buttons now sit under your Reliquary grid, the Take buttons under the Vault grid, and Sort is centered above the Reliquary grid. The Vault tabs line up with the top of the Reliquary grid, the Vault grid matches its size, and the gear panel now also shows your tool belt and potion belt.
The Vault's Sort button now sorts your bag as well as the Vault.
The "Swap spells" button at the bottom right is now called "Spellbook" and is a snugger fit.
In the Ossuary Vault you can now drag items between the Vault and your bag or worn gear, and Shift+click a stack to choose how many to move.
The "Spells" button is gone from the menu row under the minimap; the Grimoire still opens with L or the spells button by the action bar.
Vault: dragging items works now. A plain click still moves an item at once; press and drag to drop it where you want.
Vault: Shift+click now moves the amount you type (it moved the whole stack before), and Enter in the amount box moves it too.

New class, the Reaper: a fast scythe fighter with green energy that refills on its own and a soul bag that every kill fills (each soul adds 2% damage). Scythe Throw spins on a pack for 2s, Reap sweeps a huge cone, Wraith Walk rushes through enemies and curses them, Soul Burst spends the bag. It uses a borrowed hero model and class-art placeholders until its own are made.

title: A Calmer Login Screen
items: The crafting windows' "Only craftable" checkbox is now remembered between sessions.
The login and discipline screens use a still background: no more scenery swinging around with your mouse.
Login screen tidied up: the title fits on one line, the headline is tighter, the sign-in card no longer has an empty gap under the button, and the text describes the game as it is today.
Hovering your ability bar no longer pops up spell tooltips; the details stay in the Grimoire.
Clicking items in the vault (and other item grids) no longer makes your character walk toward the spot under the window.
Grimoire: the Loadouts strip no longer gets covered by the Rune socket panel.
The Reliquary has a new potion belt under the tool belt: drag a healing flask, elixir or tonic from your bag onto the Heal (Q), Elixir (Z) or Tonic (X) slot to choose what each key drinks.

title: Co-op: Thralls Leave With Their Necromancer
items: When a co-op partner leaves, their thralls now leave with them instead of staying behind in the host's world, fighting for nobody.

title: Co-op Joining Fixed
items: Joining a friend's session works again: the joiner now actually connects to the host instead of loading for a minute and failing with "The host did not answer".

title: Stairs, Fen and Loot Icons
items: Bag: the Trinket and Off hand slots are square again, and long item stat lines wrap so the window contents stay put when you select different items.
Bag: a long set-bonus line no longer stretches the Reliquary, so the bag grid stays fully visible and the window stops jumping when you pick an item.
Depths stairs look like stone stairwells with steps again, instead of a flat circle.
The Mourning Fen hummocks are muted peat mounds with a pale rim, closer to how they used to look.
Loot on the ground now shows the item's own icon (helm, chest, staff...) instead of a plain square.
Clicking the minimap shows the amber destination marker again while your hero walks there.
Bag: the Trinket and Off hand slots no longer stretch, and the window contents stay still when you select items.

title: Smoother and Faster
items: Bag: you can now drag gear from the Reliquary onto its matching character slot or tool-belt cell to equip it, and item icons keep their proportions instead of stretching.
Respawning no longer leaves your hero lying in the death pose.
Thralls animate smoothly again: anything on screen now animates every frame (they were updating at a fraction of the frame rate).
Movement of your hero, enemies, thralls and bosses is smoothed between simulation steps, so it looks fluid on 120/144 Hz screens.
Big fights cost less: enemies far from the action think less often, wave spawns are spread over a few frames, and corpses stop animating once they settle.
Textures use the GPU's compressed formats: about 75% less video memory with the same look.
Fewer shadows to draw in crowds (the nearest enemies keep theirs), and the HUD and minimap only redraw what changed.
Settings → Window mode: choose Windowed, Windowed borderless or Fullscreen.
Typing in a text field (like the bug report window) no longer moves your hero, whatever keys you have bound to movement.

title: Better Bug Reports
items: Settings → Report a bug can now attach the end of your game log, including the session that crashed if the game closed on you. It is ticked by default; untick it to leave the log out.
Before sending, your computer's user folder is hidden and anything that looks like a password or login token is blanked.
Fixes for reported bugs now show as "Fixed — live now" in your report list as soon as the update is out, and are announced in #deathmuffin.

title: One Game: the Baseline
items: Death Muffin is now one game: the Windows client from the launcher, played online. The browser version is retired.
Online is open to everyone. Sign in with your existing account; your online characters carry over.
Necromancer only for now: the four necromancer disciplines are playable. The other five are shown as Coming later while they are rebuilt properly.
A character on a discipline that is not playable yet can switch to a necromancer discipline.
Characters from the old offline edition are removed when you start the game online.
The launcher has one Play button: it downloads, updates and starts the game.
Behind the scenes: old code and documents cleared out and every test passing, so fixes and polish land faster from here.
